title: The Mountain Survival Challenge
shortDescription: A day hike turns deadly when the weather closes in. Every choice counts.
description: It was supposed to be an easy day on the Garrow Ridge Trail. Three hours from the trailhead, the sky turns the colour of slate, the wind picks up and the temperature starts to fall fast. Your phone has 20% battery and no signal. Getting home depends on the decisions you make in the next few hours: when to turn back, which way to go, and when to stop and think.

scenes.title: Clouds on the Ridge
scenes.introText: Early afternoon on Garrow Ridge. The summit hut is ninety minutes ahead; the trailhead is three hours behind. In the last twenty minutes the clouds have dropped onto the peaks, the wind has swung round to the north and your fingers are going numb inside your gloves.
scenes.outroText: A gust nearly knocks you off your feet. Somewhere above you, thunder rolls along the ridge. You need to decide now.

decisions.text: Turn back now and head down toward the trailhead
decisions.feedback: Turning back early is the single most effective survival decision in the mountains. The summit will still be there next week.

decisions.text: Push on to the summit hut. It's only ninety minutes away
decisions.feedback: Pushing higher into deteriorating weather exposes you to wind, cold and lightning, with fewer ways out.

decisions.text: Shelter under a rock overhang and wait for the storm to pass
decisions.feedback: Short-term shelter can help, but mountain storms can last for hours and daylight is limited.

scenes.title: Above the Treeline
scenes.introText: Forty minutes later the cloud swallows the ridge. Visibility drops to a few metres. The painted trail markers have disappeared under blowing snow, and you realise you haven't seen a cairn for a while.
scenes.outroText: You stop. Every direction looks the same: grey rock, grey sky, white snow.
scenes.educationalNote: In a whiteout, people often walk in circles. Stopping, using a map and compass, and returning to the last known point is safer than guessing.

decisions.text: Stop, check the map and compass, and retrace your steps to the last cairn
decisions.feedback: Returning to your last known position is exactly the right move when you lose the trail.

decisions.text: Keep walking in the direction you think the hut is
decisions.feedback: Walking on without a confirmed direction usually takes you further from help.

scenes.title: Under the Overhang
scenes.introText: The overhang keeps off the worst of the sleet, but the wind still finds you. An hour passes. The storm isn't easing, your clothes are damp, and you've started to shiver in long, uncontrollable waves.
scenes.outroText: The light is already fading. Sunset is in about two hours.
scenes.educationalNote: Uncontrollable shivering is an early sign of hypothermia. Dry layers, food and gentle movement all help your body produce heat.

decisions.text: Put on every dry layer, eat something and start down while there's still light
decisions.feedback: Fuel, insulation and movement are how your body fights off the cold. Good recovery.

decisions.text: Curl up and try to sleep until morning
decisions.feedback: Sleeping while wet and shivering, without insulation, lets hypothermia progress unnoticed.

scenes.title: The Descent
scenes.introText: You're heading down. The sleet has turned to heavy rain and the trail is running with water. At a junction a faded sign points left along the marked trail: 2.5 km of switchbacks. To the right, a steep gully of loose scree drops straight toward the valley and looks like it would save an hour.
scenes.outroText: Your knees ache and the light is going. The shortcut is very tempting.

decisions.text: Stay on the marked trail, even though it's longer
decisions.feedback: Marked trails are built to be walked safely in bad conditions, and rescuers search them first.
Wet scree is unstable and falls are common. Shortcuts off-trail also make you harder to find.

scenes.title: The Scree Gully
scenes.introText: Halfway down, the rocks shift under your boot. You slide several metres and land hard. When you try to stand, pain shoots through your right ankle. It might be broken. It's almost dark.
scenes.outroText: You're off the trail, injured, and nobody knows exactly where you are.
scenes.educationalNote: If you're injured, making yourself visible and staying warm is usually safer than moving. Three blasts on a whistle is a recognised distress signal.

decisions.text: Wrap up in your emergency blanket, blow three whistle blasts and send your location by text
decisions.feedback: Staying put, staying warm and signalling gives rescuers the best chance of finding you.

decisions.text: Try to hobble the rest of the way down in the dark
decisions.feedback: Moving in the dark on an injured ankle risks another fall and takes you further from where rescuers would look.

scenes.title: The Swollen Creek
scenes.introText: Near the bottom of the valley you hear it before you see it: Garrow Creek, brown and roaring. The footbridge you crossed this morning has been torn away. The trailhead car park is just two hundred metres beyond the far bank.
scenes.outroText: The water is knee-deep near the edge and moving fast. Your car is so close.
scenes.educationalNote: Fast-moving water only 15 cm deep can knock an adult over. Look for a wide, shallow, slow section, or wait for the water to drop.

decisions.text: Follow the bank upstream to find a wider, shallower place to cross
decisions.feedback: Wide sections of a river are shallower and slower. Patience here saves lives.

decisions.text: Wade straight across. The car is right there
decisions.feedback: Crossing a flooded creek at its narrowest point is where the current is strongest.

scenes.title: Back at the Trailhead
scenes.introText: Ten minutes upstream the creek spreads out over a gravel bar, shin-deep and slow. You unclip your pack's hip belt, face upstream and shuffle across. Twenty minutes later you're sitting in your car with the heater roaring, watching the storm swallow the ridge you were standing on.

ending.title: Safe and Sound
ending.summary: You read the danger early and made steady, careful choices all the way down.

scenes.title: Lights on the Mountain
scenes.introText: Your text gets through during a brief gap in the cloud. Just after midnight, headlamps appear on the slope below and a voice calls your name. The search and rescue team splints your ankle and helps you down. It's a long night, but you're going home.

ending.title: Rescued
ending.summary: The shortcut cost you, but staying put and signalling brought help to you.

scenes.title: Lost in the Storm
scenes.introText: You keep moving, sure that the way out is just ahead. It isn't. By the time the storm clears the next morning you are kilometres from the trail, exhausted and hypothermic. A helicopter crew spots you by chance. You survive, but only just.

ending.title: Lost
ending.summary: Moving without knowing where you were going took you away from safety.

scenes.title: The Long Night
scenes.introText: You drift in and out of an uneasy sleep. The shivering stops, and you start to feel strangely warm, which is one of the most dangerous signs of all. Rescuers find you the next afternoon, severely hypothermic.

ending.title: Hypothermia
ending.summary: Waiting in wet clothes without warmth or food let the cold win.

scenes.title: Swept Away
scenes.introText: Three steps in, the current rips your feet out from under you. You're carried fifty metres downstream before you grab a fallen branch and drag yourself back to the bank you started from, soaked, bruised and freezing, with night falling.

ending.title: Swept Away
ending.summary: Floodwater is far stronger than it looks. Crossing at the narrowest point was the riskiest choice.

achievements.title: Wilderness Survivor
achievements.description: Walk out of the mountains on your own by reaching the trailhead safely.

achievements.title: Quick Thinker
achievements.description: Get injured off-trail, then signal effectively so that rescuers can find you.

achievements.title: Excellent Decision Maker
achievements.description: Make three best-possible decisions in a single run of the Mountain Survival Challenge.

achievements.title: Perfect Survival Run
achievements.description: Reach a safe ending having made the best choice at every decision point.

achievements.title: Mountain Explorer
achievements.description: Discover every ending of the Mountain Survival Challenge.
